text: The Ombudsman Toronto report (Item CC30.3 , May 22, 2025) underscores gaps in tenant protection in multi-tenant homes, disproportionately affecting Black, Indigenous, and racialized residents. Disaggregated race-based data collection is essential for identifying systemic barriers and informing equitable housing policy. CABRAC has a mandate to advance data-driven approaches that address anti-Black racism.

The Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee: 1. Recommended that the Economic and Community Development Committee request the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Unit, Social Development to invite Toronto Community Housing to provide to the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee a presentation on initiatives to collect and analyze disaggregated race-based data on evictions, arrears, and tenant relocations. 2. Recommended that the Economic and Community Development Committee request the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Unit, Social Development to invite Toronto Community Housing and the Housing Secretariat to provide to the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee a presentation and a summary of programs currently addressing evictions by the first quarter of 2026, including equity-based data, including race and gender, collected through various Toronto Community Housing…
